lines.text: Have you ever explored an older American house and spotted a mysterious tiny door near the floor?
No, they weren't built for secret pets or tiny fairy visitors.
In the early twentieth century, these small exterior-facing hatches were milk delivery doors.
Every morning, local milkmen placed fresh glass bottles of cold milk into the insulated compartment from outside.
Families could open the interior latch from the kitchen without ever stepping outside into winter snow.
Other floor-level doors led to coal chutes or laundry chutes dropping straight into the basement furnace room.
These vintage doors are charming relics of everyday American life before modern grocery stores.
